title: Menaka’s Keema Matar

items.raw: 1 tablespoon each grated fresh ginger and garlic
2 teaspoons ground coriander, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, ½ teaspoon turmeric
1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili powder or paprika
2 ripe tomatoes, finely chopped (or 1 cup canned crushed)
Chopped cilantro and lime wedges, to serve

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide heavy pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until deep golden. Their color sets the color of the whole dish.
Stir in the ginger, garlic, and chilies and cook 1 to 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone.
Add the meat and break it up well. Cook over medium-high 6 to 8 minutes until no pink remains and the juices have mostly cooked off.
Add the ground spices and cook 1 minute, then the tomatoes and salt. Cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Stir in the peas and ½ cup water. Cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala, taste for salt, and scatter with cilantro. Serve with rice or warm roti and lime wedges.

notes.label: Patience with the onions
notes.text: pale onions make a pale, flat keema. Take them all the way to golden brown.

notes.label: Heat
notes.text: Kashmiri chili gives color more than fire. Add heat with the green chilies.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: keeps 4 days in the refrigerator and freezes well; the flavor deepens overnight.

openQuestion: Tell me about Menaka and this dish — when did she first make it for the family, and when does it show up now? Does she use lamb, beef, or chicken, and does she add potatoes or yogurt?
